title: Agentic artificial intelligence-driven tutoring: A multi-agent cognitive architecture for personalized adaptive learning in Education
venue: International Journal of Applied Resilience and Sustainability
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of delivering personalized and adaptive instruction in education, arguing that conventional one-size-fits-all teaching cannot adequately meet diverse learner needs, especially in large classes and fast-changing knowledge domains. It reviews the literature on agentic AI-driven tutoring systems, focusing on multi-agent cognitive architectures that aim to model learner cognition, behavior, affect, and metacognition to support more responsive instruction than traditional educational software.

The paper is a PRISMA-based systematic review of recent research on intelligent tutoring systems, multi-agent systems, cognitive computing, and adaptive learning technologies. It synthesizes studies across educational contexts, including mathematics, science, language learning, programming, and professional training, rather than reporting a single primary intervention with a participant sample. The review examines design elements such as pedagogical agents, learner modeling, feedback generation, affective computing, metacognitive scaffolding, collaborative learning support, learning analytics, and domain-specific applications.

The main conclusion is that multi-agent AI tutoring systems can offer more fine-grained personalization, real-time feedback, adaptive scaffolding, and richer learner modeling than traditional learning technologies. The paper also emphasizes key barriers to implementation, including privacy, transparency, scalability, teacher integration, and the need for stronger evaluation frameworks. Overall, it frames agentic AI tutoring as a promising direction for education while calling for more rigorous, ethical, and scalable development and assessment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative/systematic review article rather than an empirical study, and it does not report original experimental evaluation of a baseline versus intervention. It therefore provides no direct causal evidence on outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact estimate is reported because the paper is conceptual and review-based, with no measurable effect sizes or comparative learning outcomes. The article discusses potential benefits of AI tutoring systems but does not demonstrate observed impact.

interventions.use_case: review of agentic AI-driven multi-agent cognitive tutoring architectures for personalized adaptive learning, including learner modeling, feedback, scaffolding, metacognitive support, and adaptive instructional planning
adaptive learning systems that personalize content, pacing, scaffolding, and feedback based on learner state and performance
automated feedback generation for student answers, writing, and problem solving, including template-based, case-based, and natural-language feedback
learning analytics and predictive modeling to forecast performance, dropout risk, and learner trajectories from interaction data
conversational tutoring interfaces and dialogue management for natural-language instructional interaction
